definitions.explanation: A Japanese street food made from batter cooked in a fish-shaped (specifically sea bream) mold, typically filled with sweet red bean paste. Other common fillings include custard, chocolate, and cheese.

examples.japanese: {鯛焼|たいや}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{焼|や}きたて→焼きたて：16735_yakitate⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鯛焼|たいや}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦パリッとしていた→パリッとする：26984_parittosuru⟧。
examples.english: The freshly baked taiyaki had a crispy outside.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鯛焼|たいや}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{餡子|あんこ}→餡子：08654_anko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦しっぽ→しっぽ：09089_shippo⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦ぎっしり→ぎっしり：05891_gisshiri⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: The taiyaki at that shop is packed with red bean paste all the way to the tail.

notes:
KANJI: ⟦{鯛|たい}→鯛：14709_tai⟧ means sea bream, ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ means grilled/baked. The name comes from the fish shape of the mold.

CULTURAL NOTES: A popular street food and festival snack. The classic filling is ⟦{餡子|あんこ}→餡子：08654_anko⟧ (sweet red bean paste), but modern variations include custard cream, chocolate, cheese, and savory fillings. There is a long-running debate about whether to eat from the head or the tail first.
